headline: Viral Theory Connects 'Birds Aren't Real' Movement to Ohio's Alleged Non-Existence
subheadline: Conspiracy theorists claim both phenomena share 'suspicious origin point' in 1997
summary: Internet researchers have drawn connections between two separate conspiracy theories, suggesting a unified explanation for both.
content:
A Threadit post titled "Birds and Ohio: The Connection They Don't Want You to See" has accumulated 23,000 upvotes after proposing that two seemingly unrelated conspiracy theories are actually the same conspiracy.

The "Birds Aren't Real" movement, which claims birds were replaced by government surveillance drones in the 1970s, has long been a fixture of internet culture. Separately, the "Ohio Isn't Real" theory suggests the midwestern state is a fabrication maintained through mass hypnosis and doctored maps.

Now, user u/ConnectingDots847 claims to have found the link.

"Where do birds migrate in winter? They don't say. Where is Ohio supposedly located? Right in the middle of major migration routes," the post reads. "Birds fly 'through' Ohio. But if Ohio isn't real, where are they actually going? Nowhere. Because they're not real either. It's all the same cover-up."

The theory proposes that Ohio was invented as a fictional waypoint to explain bird migration patterns. "You need somewhere for the fake birds to go," u/ConnectingDots847 explains. "So you invent a fake state. It's elegant, really."

Skeptics point out that Ohio has 11.8 million residents, professional sports teams, and a robust economy. Believers counter that "that's exactly what they'd want you to think" and that anyone claiming to be from Ohio is "either lying or doesn't realize they're actually from Indiana."

Dr. Patricia Huang, when asked to comment, sighed for approximately 8 seconds before responding: "I've been asked to weigh in on a lot of things. This is the one that broke me."

The post has spawned r/BirdsAndOhio, which already has 8,470 members. Their slogan: "Two lies. One truth. Wake up."
author: Marcus Webb, Internet Culture Correspondent
